MAJOR: `audit_hold_guard` inserts the spoliation event and then `RAISE EXCEPTION` in the same transaction: the raise rolls back the event insert, so `audit_hold_after_purge_total`'s DB evidence is never persisted, and no Go path ever increments `MetricHoldAfterPurge` (or InsertOutOfRange/ProvisionSeconds/LateInsert/HoldExtractFailed) — AC "rejected and emits" is unmet.

AC's hold-reconcile flow (hold placed AFTER archive → restore to scratch, extract, verify) has no implementation in Go or SQL; `audit_approve_purge`/`audit_drop_partition` only reject active holds, they never reconcile already-archived months.

`VerifyHoldExtraction` digest-compare breaks with more than one hold on a month: the archive stores one copy per hold, so `archSum != liveSum` even when extraction is complete — retention is permanently blocked for multiply-held months.

No EDP service startup check or ops cron emitting `audit_partition_months_ahead` / `audit_partition_low_coverage_total` appears in the diff; only the `pfaudit-retention coverage` CLI does, so the AC's non-fatally-surfaced stale-coverage alert is unwired.

No statement-level TRUNCATE deny trigger exists on `audit_partitioned` or `audit_legal_hold_archive` (only on the two events tables); `REVOKE TRUNCATE` is ineffective for the owner, so `pf_owner` can still wipe the audit journal.

`CheckSSE` unconditionally rejects bare `"aws:kms"`, which is exactly what `DefaultSSE()` returns whenever `PF_S3_BUCKET` is set without a KMS key — S3 archive/backup is dead-on-arrival unless `PF_S3_KMS_KEY` is set, contradicting the comment "defaults to AES256".

AC's `audit_late_YYYYMM` bounded late partitions were dropped entirely (late rows go into the canonical month); the "strictly below grace, non-overlapping, cannot satisfy coverage" requirement and its tests are silently unimplemented.
MINOR: `PurgeMonth` re-run resets the purge timestamp (`audit_mark_purged` unconditionally sets `purged_at = now()`), silently restarting the audit clock on resume after a partial failure.
`Append`'s 23514 classification matches on the English substring "no partition of relation" — locale/version fragile; a stable SQLSTATE+constraint-name check would be robust.
`Rehearsal` comment claims RLS policies are asserted in the dump listing, but only table and sequence names are checked.
AC "fresh-install (empty audit, setval to 1) case tested" has no test; §17's early RETURN on a fresh install is unexercised.
The integration test attaches a partition with a raw `CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF`, contradicting the "attach is the only supported path" invariant the same suite enforces elsewhere.
`Rehearsal`/`backup` shell out to `age` and `pg_restore` with no version/path pinning or existence check surfaced early — an ops box without them fails at the worst moment (post-swap close gate).
`audit_provision` comment says "the trigger is cloned onto every leaf"; it is only on the parent — misleading for future hardening changes.
Unknown-size S3 puts leave `Info.Checksum`/`Version` empty; nothing verifies the backup object's integrity at rest (only size > 0).
NIT: `architect-review.json` reformatting (arrays exploded) is unrelated churn in a config gate file.
`emitMetrics`/`activeMetrics` globals in `pfaudit-swap` are redundant with the `fail()` parameter already carrying state; a plain struct field would do.
`metrics.go` `Inc` creates the counter under lock then increments atomically outside — correct but the map-of-pointers design invites a copy bug later.
`TestUnhardenedLeafDetected` uses `2100 + nano%200` as a year to dodge collisions; a UUID-suffixed month with an explicit teardown would be less surprising.
SUMMARY: Solid substrate: ensure-based DDL, catalog-driven swap resume, bounded S4 freeze with in-lock delta re-count, and privilege-enforced hardening are genuinely well designed and tested.

Top risks are legal/compliance completeness rather than mechanics: the spoliation event is rolled back with the rejected insert, hold-reconcile is entirely missing, multi-hold months wedge retention, and the coverage/late-insert observability ACs are uninstrumented.

The SSE-KMS fail-closed logic is self-contradictory (S3 archives cannot currently be written without a KMS key despite the "AES256 default" contract), and owner-level TRUNCATE remains possible on the audit journal.
Recommend closing the AC gaps above before Gate sign-off; the core swap/retention architecture itself is sound.
